skill.name: scenario-testing
skill.description: Guides AI coding agents to validate features with scenario-driven tests that exercise real dependencies and document repeatable coverage.
skill.summary: Validate code changes with scenario tests, real dependencies, and repeatable scenario records.
skill.author: 2389-research

security_audit.summary: All static analyzer matches for Ruby or shell backtick execution are false positives caused by Markdown inline-code formatting. The system reconnaissance matches are also false positives, but the skill does have a medium contextual risk because it encourages real credential requests and real service execution without clear safeguards.

remediation.suggestion: Tell users to use sandbox credentials, avoid sharing secrets in chat, and rely on approved secret managers or local environment variables.
Require explicit user approval before hitting external services, databases, or APIs, and mention cost and data exposure risks.
Allow safe fakes when real dependencies are unavailable or risky, then require real scenario validation before release.

semantic_findings.title: Encourages Real Credential Requests
semantic_findings.description: The skill requires external APIs to hit actual services and says to ask a human partner for real API credentials. This guidance can pressure users to disclose credentials and run costly or sensitive external operations without explicit safeguards.

content.value_statement: Feature work can pass shallow tests while failing against real systems. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to prove behavior with scenario tests and documented real-dependency checks.
actual_capabilities: Directs agents to create scenario tests in a .scratch/ workspace.
Requires tests to exercise real systems and real dependencies.
Defines when a scenario is invalid because it uses mocks or fake data.
Promotes repeatable scenario patterns into a committed scenarios.jsonl file.
Sets a definition of done for scenario validation before completion.
limitations: Does not provide executable test runner code or framework adapters.
May require sandbox services, test databases, or approved credentials.
Real dependency testing can increase runtime, cost, and setup effort.
The .scratch/ scenarios are intended to stay uncommitted.

use_cases.title: Validate Backend Feature Behavior
use_cases.description: Create a real dependency scenario before marking a new API, workflow, or database-backed change as complete.

use_cases.title: Turn Bug Fixes into Repeatable Coverage
use_cases.description: Reproduce a reported failure, verify the fix with a scenario, and document the pattern for future regression checks.

use_cases.title: Guide AI Agents During Delivery
use_cases.description: Keep Claude, Codex, or Claude Code focused on proving working behavior instead of stopping at isolated unit tests.

prompt_templates.title: Create a First Scenario
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner validation for a new feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Use scenario-testing to design a .scratch/ scenario for this feature. Include the real dependencies it must exercise and the pass condition.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a Bug Fix
prompt_templates.prompt: Use scenario-testing to reproduce this bug with real dependencies, verify the fix, and list what makes the scenario independent.

prompt_templates.title: Promote a Scenario Pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Use scenario-testing to extract the validated scenario into a scenarios.jsonl entry with name, given, when, then, and validates fields.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Release Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Use scenario-testing to review this change set for missing real-dependency scenarios, invalid mock usage, and unresolved validation gaps.

output_examples.input: Validate a user registration workflow before release.
output_examples.output: A .scratch/ scenario plan that uses the real database, real auth service in test mode, expected success criteria, and cleanup notes.

output_examples.input: Convert a recurring checkout validation into shared coverage.
output_examples.output: A documented scenario pattern with a clear given, when, then flow and a list of business behavior it validates.

output_examples.input: Review a completed bug fix for missing validation.
output_examples.output: A gap report that names missing real-dependency checks, invalid mocks, and the scenario needed before declaring the fix complete.

best_practices: Use sandbox or test-mode services when real external systems are required.
Keep each scenario independent so it can run alone and in parallel.
Move stable lessons from scratch scenarios into committed scenario documentation.
anti_patterns: Treating mocked unit tests as proof that a feature works end to end.
Running scenarios that depend on hidden state from earlier test executions.
Requesting or exposing production secrets instead of approved test credentials.

faq.question: Does this skill write test code for me?
faq.answer: It gives process guidance and scenario structure. The agent still adapts implementation details to your project and test framework.

faq.question: Can I use mocks with this skill?
faq.answer: The skill rejects mocks as final validation. Use real dependencies or approved sandbox equivalents for completion evidence.

faq.question: What is .scratch/ used for?
faq.answer: .scratch/ is a temporary workspace for scenario experiments. The skill expects it to remain ignored by version control.

faq.question: What should go into scenarios.jsonl?
faq.answer: Put repeatable scenario patterns there after they prove useful. Include the behavior, setup, action, expected result, and validation purpose.

faq.question: Does this require production services?
faq.answer: No. Use sandbox, test-mode, or staging services when possible, and get explicit approval before touching real external systems.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
